newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt reaches agreement on Euro-tax plan.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt reaches agreement on Euro-tax plan.

text.p: The Italian centre-left government said on Friday it had reached an agreement between its coalition partners over controversial "Euro-tax" proposals.
"We have reached an agreement," deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni told reporters after a meeting in the senate (upper house) that ended shortly after midnight.
Veltroni said the government had listened to the Senate party leaders and had "formulated a proposal on which there is agreement."
He said the government would look at the technical details again on Friday and Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco would put forward more detailed proposals.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi said the modifications included raising the tax threshold for the self-employed to bringing them more in line with the employed.
"It was a technical adjustment, not a revolution," Prodi declared after the meeting. "Right from the start I said I was not just willing but extremely open.
"The problem was to get the same amount, not hit general principles and the amendments were made seriously and without problems," he said.

Asked whether he thought Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, whose small centrist Italian Renewal party was the main objector to the government's original amendment first put forward on Wednesday, Prodi replied: "I think so."
Ottaviano Del Turco, a member of Dini's party at the meeting, said his party was satisfied.

"There has been a very important coming together. I think that the government's sensitivity, which with Veltroni, Prodi and Visco has wanted to take into account the feelings of the coalition, has obtained an important result."

The 12.5 trillion lire ($8.3 billion) Euro-tax is a key piece of Prodi's tough 1997 budget, which aims to prune 62.5 trillion lire off next year's deficit and spur Italy's hopes of joining economic and monetary union (EMU) from the start. Rome newsroom +396-6782505
